main_text.l: gulorum planorum & solidorum: nam angulos planos
vocant Winckel, angulos solidos vocant Ranten.
Solidum planum est vel Pyramis, vel
Prisma.
Pyramis est solidum planum à basi
recti linea ad verticem vsque æqualibus
triangulis fastigiatum.
Euclides libro 11. prop. 12. sic definit: Pyra-
mis est figura solida, quæ planis continetur,
ab vno plano ad vnum punctum constituta.
Prisma est corpus sex superficiebus comprehen-
sum, cuius duo opposita sunt æqualia & parallela,
reliqua autem parallelogramma.
Prisma est à πρίσμα quod significat secor: itaque pri-
sma est tabula secta sive mensa & asser; unde etiam à
Campano Corpus Serratile dicitur. Clavius lib. 11. prop. 13:
Prisma definit, quod ni-
hil sit aliud, quam co-
lumna quædam laterata
æqualis crassitudinis,
cuius bases oppositæ sunt
æquales, similes & paral-
lelæ, sive hæ sint triangulæ
sive quadrangulæ sive
quinquangulæ &c. Pingitur in tali figura:
Tantum de corporibus regularibus simplici-
bus: Composita sive mixta sunt, quæ etsi basin
circulare habeant, varia tamen planitie constant.
Ex his alia possunt esse Principalia alia minus
principalia.
Principalia sunt quinque illa corpora valde
celebrata apud Mathematicos: nempe Cubus,
Tetraedron, Octoedron, Dodecaedron &
Icosaedron.
Vocantur hæc quinque corpora vere principaliter imo

page.notes: Figure captions: "Pyramis" beside the pyramid figure; "Prisma" above the prism figure. Last line is partly cut by the page edge and the word "imo" is printed at the line end; the catchword-like mark "I" below the last line is a signature-type mark and is omitted. Several Greek words (πρίσμα) and the German words Winckel and Ranten are in black letter in the original and were copied as shown.
